title: Research Fellow - DLMP - Algeciras-Schimnich lab
description:
A Research Fellow position is available in the Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathology at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team focused on translating novel biomarkers of Alzheimer disease and neurodegeneration from research into clinical practice.

The position will support studies within the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging and the Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center, integrating basic research, clinical laboratory medicine, assay evaluation, and biomarker interpretation. Areas of focus include biomarkers for the diagnosis, staging, and prognosis of Alzheimer disease and related dementias.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Design and conduct clinical and translational research studies focused on Alzheimer disease biomarkers and related neurodegenerative disease biomarkers.

  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including laboratory medicine professionals, neurologists, neuropsychologists, statisticians, bioinformaticians, and clinical researchers.

  • Contribute to manuscript preparation, abstract submissions, scientific presentations, grant applications, and development of figures and tables for publication.

  • Maintain accurate records of study design, analytical methods, data analyses, and regulatory or protocol-related documentation.

  • Mentor junior research staff, trainees, or students as appropriate and contribute to a collaborative and rigorous research environment.

Research Projects:

  • Assessment of blood biomarkers for Alzheimer disease diagnosis, prognosis, and clinical implementation.

  • Evaluation of assay performance and sources of variability affecting biomarker measurement and interpretation.

  • Development of biomarker-based prediction and risk models incorporating clinical and demographic variables.

  • Studies addressing preanalytical factors, assay harmonization, reference intervals, and reporting strategies for neurodegenerative disease biomarkers.

  • Translation of biomarker research findings into clinically actionable laboratory testing frameworks.

A Research Fellow position in Life Sciences (LS) will require knowledge of either clinical-based research or laboratory-based research often obtained from a postdoctoral program.

A Research Fellow at Mayo Clinic is a temporary position intended to provide training and education in research. Individuals will train in the research program of a Mayo Clinic principal investigator. Qualified individuals will demonstrate the potential for research as evidenced by their training and peer-reviewed publications and should become competitive for national research grants. Proof of English proficiency is required for J-1 Short-Term Scholars, Research Scholars, Professors, Specialists, and Student Interns sponsored by Mayo Clinic.

Ph.D. in neuroscience, neurology, biology, biochemistry, clinical chemistry, laboratory medicine, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Alzheimer disease or neurodegenerative disease biomarker research.

  • Strong quantitative skills, including experience with statistical analysis of clinical or laboratory data.

  • Familiarity with clinical laboratory quality standards, assay performance evaluation, or regulatory expectations is desirable, but not required.

  • Demonstrated scientific productivity through peer-reviewed publications, abstracts, or conference presentations.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and ability to work independently and collaboratively.

Application Materials:

Qualified candidates should submit a curriculum vitae, a brief statement of research interests and career goals, and contact information for three references. Candidates should describe relevant experience in biomarker research, clinical laboratory medicine, assay development or validation, statistical analysis, or neurodegenerative disease research.

title: Medior PHP Backend Developer
description:
About Shiftbase

At Shiftbase, we build workforce software that helps people get work done. Thousands of teams across Europe rely on our platform every day to plan work, track time, and manage leave. We reduce admin so businesses can focus on what really matters.

About Shiftbase

At Shiftbase, we build workforce software that helps people get work done. Thousands of teams across Europe rely on our platform every day to plan work, track time, and manage leave. We reduce admin so businesses can focus on what really matters. Our engineering team is 18 people, a mix of cultures and backgrounds, working in an open team culture where ideas travel freely regardless of title.

About The Role

You'd join a backend group of 7 engineers, most of them senior, working on a platform that serves hundreds of thousands of users daily. This is not a greenfield project. Our codebase has real history and real complexity. We're actively modernizing it: migrating to Symfony, implementing hexagonal architecture, using DDD principles, running on GCP with Kubernetes and Flux, and generating API contracts with OpenAPI. You'll help drive these improvements and take ownership of meaningful parts of the system. The domain is complex. Workforce management touches scheduling, time tracking, leave policies, and labor law across multiple countries. Even our senior engineers take time to fully understand it. If that kind of depth excites you rather than intimidates you, keep reading.

What makes this role different

You'll deepen your engineering craft, not just write code.Yes, we use PHP (latest version) with Symfony. But the real value here is applying and sharpening your skills in OOP, SOLID, Hexagonal Architecture, and Domain-Driven Design. These are transferable principles that make you a strong engineer in any language or stack. You'll be part of an experienced team that values quality.You'll collaborate closely with senior engineers through meaningful code reviews, architectural discussions, and pair programming. You'll also be in a position to mentor less experienced developers and help raise the bar across the team. You'll work with AI tooling that most companies won't adopt for years.We're heavily invested in AI-assisted development. Everyone has access to the latest models. We use Claude Code as our primary tool, we're building spec-driven development workflows, and we're targeting 80% AI-generated code. You'd be developing software in a way that will define how engineering works going forward.

Your first 90 days

We have a structured 30/60/90 onboarding plan. You'll get a buddy, guided first work items, and the context you need to start making an impact quickly. By the end of your first quarter, you'll own features end to end and contribute to technical decisions within the team.

What you'll do

  • Build and ship backend features that directly impact users
  • Improve performance, reliability, and scalability of existing systems
  • Break down complex problems into well-structured, testable solutions
  • Drive modernization efforts: refactoring legacy code safely and pragmatically
  • Design and optimize relational database queries and data models
  • Participate actively in code reviews, architecture discussions, and technical decision-making
  • Use AI development tools as part of your daily workflow
  • Help mentor junior developers and share knowledge within the team

Career growth

We use a skill matrix to plot a clear development path, including personal goals you set yourself. You'll have regular growth conversations and a concrete picture of what you're working toward. This role is a strong stepping stone toward a senior engineering position.

Who are we looking for

People who are genuinely curious. Who constantly come with ideas to improve things. Who want to try new approaches and aren't afraid to challenge the status quo. Who find satisfaction in making a complex system better over time.

You might be a great fit if:

  • You have a few years of professional experience in backend development (roughly 3–5 years)
  • You're proficient in PHP and comfortable working with Symfony or a similar framework
  • You have solid experience with relational databases and RESTful APIs
  • You're familiar with principles like SOLID, clean architecture, or domain-driven design — and you actively try to apply them
  • You're comfortable with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and writing automated tests
  • You take ownership of your work and proactively propose improvements - You're curious about how systems work under the hood and always looking to grow

It helps if you've worked with AI development tools, contributed to modernization or migration projects, or have experience with event-driven architectures or cloud infrastructure. Note: Candidates outside the Netherlands will not be considered

title: Project Manager I
description:
The Project Manager is a professional-level position that provides operational, regulatory, and administrative leadership for a federally funded clinical research study under the direction of Principal Investigator (PI) Dr. Theresa Beckie. This soft-funded, five-year position is responsible for coordinating all aspects of study implementation, including participant recruitment and retention, regulatory compliance, protocol execution, staff supervision, data management, quality assurance, and inter-institutional collaboration.

The incumbent independently manages daily study operations, ensures adherence to federal regulations and institutional policies governing human subjects research, coordinates activities across multiple study sites, and serves as the primary operational liaison among investigators, research staff, study participants, collaborating institutions, and funding agencies. The position exercises considerable judgment in managing study activities, maintaining protocol fidelity, resolving operational issues, and ensuring the integrity and quality of research data.

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg and USF Health. In 2025, U.S. News & World Report recognized USF with its highest overall ranking in university history, as a top 50 public university for the seventh consecutive year and as one of the top 15 best values among all public universities in the nation. U.S. News also ranks the USF Health Morsani College of Medicine in the highest tier, placing it as one of the top 16 medical schools in the nation and inside the top 10 among public universities. USF is a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), a group that includes only the top 3% of universities in the U.S. With an all-time high of $750 million in research funding in 2025 and as a top 20 public university for producing U.S. patents, USF uses innovation to transform lives and shape a better future. The university generates an annual economic impact of nearly $10 billion for the state of Florida. USF’s Division I athletics teams compete in the American Conference. Learn more at .

This position is grant-funded and time-limited, with up to a 5-year contract.

Study Management and Regulatory Oversight (40%)

Provides leadership and day-to-day operational management of a five-year federally funded clinical research study. Coordinates and monitors all study activities to ensure compliance with approved protocols, funding agency requirements, Good Clinical Practice standards, and institutional policies.

Plans, coordinates, and oversees participant recruitment, screening, enrollment, randomization, informed consent procedures, study visits, retention activities, and follow-up assessments.

Prepares, submits, and maintains regulatory documentation, including Institutional Review Board (IRB) applications, amendments, continuing reviews, adverse event reports, protocol deviations, and study correspondence. Serves as the primary contact for regulatory matters and ensures completion of all required regulatory reporting.

Monitors study progress and operational performance, identifies issues affecting study implementation, and develops corrective action plans to maintain compliance, participant safety, and study objectives.

Coordinates study meetings, tracks milestones and deliverables, and assists with budget monitoring and financial documentation to support effective study management.

Protocol Implementation, Data Management, and Quality Assurance (40%)

Directs implementation of study protocols and procedures across participating research sites to ensure standardization and consistency of study activities.

Coordinates procurement, inventory management, and distribution of study supplies, intervention materials, and equipment necessary for study implementation.

Oversees participant assessments, intervention delivery, and data collection activities. Ensures accurate, complete, and timely collection and management of research data in accordance with study protocols and federal requirements.

Maintains quality assurance and quality control procedures to safeguard data integrity and participant safety. Conducts ongoing review of study processes and recommends procedural improvements to enhance study efficiency and data quality.

Provides participant education and training regarding study procedures and the use of digital health technologies, including smartphone- and smartwatch-based applications utilized within the research protocol.

Prepares data safety monitoring reports and other required study documentation. Interprets and applies federal, state, institutional, and sponsor regulations governing human subjects research.

Coordinates study activities with investigators, research staff, and collaborating institutions to ensure successful implementation and achievement of study objectives.

Personnel Leadership and Supervision (15%)

Recruits, trains, supervises, and evaluates study personnel, including research nurses, health coaches, graduate student workers, research assistants, and study volunteers.

Develops and implements training programs to ensure consistent application of study protocols, participant safety procedures, regulatory requirements, and data collection methods across all study personnel and study sites.

Provides ongoing performance oversight and mentorship to study staff. Conducts quality assurance reviews and intervention fidelity assessments to ensure adherence to established protocols and standardized intervention delivery.

Coordinates activities among multiple study sites to ensure consistent implementation of research procedures and data collection practices.

Stakeholder Relations and Collaboration (4%)

Establishes and maintains effective working relationships with investigators, collaborating institutions, university departments, community partners, research participants, and federal funding agencies.

Serves as a liaison among research stakeholders to facilitate communication, coordination of activities, and successful completion of project objectives.

Administrative Support (1%)

Performs administrative duties in support of study operations, including document preparation, electronic record maintenance, filing, copying, scanning, and other routine office functions.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

Directly supervises research personnel, including:

  • Research Nurse
  • Health Coach
  • Graduate Student Workers
  • Research Assistants
  • Study Volunteers

Responsibilities include hiring recommendations, onboarding, training, work assignment, performance monitoring, protocol oversight, and ongoing supervision of study-related activities

This position requires a Bachelor’s degree in a related field and 2 years of project management or coordination experience; Some positions may require project management certification.

Degree Equivalency Clause: Four years of direct experience for a bachelor’s degree.
• Senate Bill 1310- The Florida Senate (https://www.flsenate.gov/Session/Bill/2023/1310) is conditional upon meeting all employment eligibility requirements in the U.S.
• SB 1310: Substitution of Work Experience for Postsecondary Education Requirements
• A public employer may include a postsecondary degree as a baseline requirement only as an alternative to the number of years of direct experience required, not to exceed:
• (a) Two years of direct experience for an associate degree;
• (b) Four years of direct experience for a bachelor’s degree;
• (c) Six years of direct experience for a master’s degree;
• (d) Seven years of direct experience for a professional degree; or
• (e) Nine years of direct experience for a doctoral degree
• Related work experience may not substitute for any required licensure, certification, or registration required for the position of employment as established by the public employer and indicated in the advertised description of the position of employment.
• Minimum Qualifications that require a high school diploma are exempt from SB 1310.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Nursing, Public Health, Health Sciences, Exercise Science, Psychology, or a related health field.
  • Experience coordinating federally funded clinical, behavioral, or translational research studies.
  • Knowledge of human subjects research regulations, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and Institutional Review Board processes.
  • Experience working with cardiovascular disease populations and women's health research.
  • Experience managing research studies from initiation through closeout.
  • Professional research certification (ACRP, SOCRA, or equivalent) preferred.
  • Experience using electronic health records, REDCap, and electronic data capture systems.
  • Demonstrated project management, organizational, leadership, and communication skills.

title: Senior Director of Product - Strategy and Growth
description:
At Intelex, we are committed to empowering organizations to manage environmental, safety, and quality concerns while reducing their social, environmental, and human impacts. We provide advanced software solutions that help businesses around the world ensure compliance, reduce risk, and improve performance. As a global leader in Environmental, Health, Safety, and Quality (EHSQ) software, Intelex is continuing its mission to build sustainable business solutions that have real-world impact.

We are seeking a strategic and commercially driven Senior Director of Product to own Intelex's inorganic growth agenda — including selective M&A opportunities, technology partnerships, and product strategy — alongside the company's market intelligence and competitive intelligence functions. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of product, strategy, and business development, shaping how Intelex grows beyond its organic product portfolio.

Position Overview

As the Senior Director/VP of Product - Strategy and Growth, you will be Intelex's primary decision-maker and owner for all inorganic growth activity and external technology relationships. You will lead the identification, evaluation, and execution of acquisition targets, technology partnerships, and strategic alliances that expand Intelex's product capabilities, addressable market, and competitive differentiation.

In parallel, you will build and own Intelex's market and competitive intelligence capability — establishing the systems, processes, and analytical frameworks that ensure every product, sales, and go-to-market decision is grounded in the best available external data. You will synthesize intelligence from customers, competitors, analysts, and market signals into actionable strategic insights that shape Intelex's roadmap, positioning, and investment priorities.

This role is ideal for a strategically minded leader with experience spanning product management, corporate development, or strategy consulting, who brings deep knowledge of the EHSQ, or adjacent enterprise software markets.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategy and Inorganic Growth

  • Own Intelex's inorganic growth strategy end-to-end — from opportunity identification through due diligence, recommendation, and post-close integration planning.
  • Define acquisition criteria aligned to Intelex's product strategy, target markets, and technology gaps, in collaboration with the CPTO and executive leadership.
  • Build and maintain a proprietary pipeline of acquisition targets and strategic investment opportunities, drawing on market intelligence, analyst relationships, and industry networks.
  • Lead product and technology due diligence on acquisition candidates, assessing product-market fit, technology architecture, customer base quality, and integration complexity.
  • Partner with Corporate Development, Finance, and Legal to structure and execute transactions, ensuring product strategy alignment throughout the deal process.

  • Own post-acquisition product integration planning — defining roadmap integration, product rationalization, and combined go-to-market strategy for acquired assets.

2. Technology Partnerships and Alliance Strategy

  • Own all decisions on technology partnerships, including API integrations, OEM agreements, co-sell arrangements, and platform ecosystem relationships.
  • Identify and prioritize technology partners that expand Intelex's capabilities, distribution reach, or competitive positioning — including ISVs, data providers, AI/ML vendors, and regulatory content partners.
  • Lead partnership negotiations and structure commercial terms in collaboration with Legal and Finance, ensuring partnerships deliver measurable product and revenue value.
  • Build and govern the Intelex technology partner ecosystem, defining tiering, onboarding standards, joint roadmap commitments, and partner performance criteria.
  • Manage senior-level partner relationships, including executive alignment, roadmap co-development, and go-to-market collaboration with strategic partners.

  • Evaluate build vs. buy vs. partner decisions for new product capabilities, providing structured recommendations to the CPTO and product leadership team.

3. Market Intelligence and Competitive Intelligence

  • Build and own Intelex's market intelligence and competitive intelligence function — establishing the processes, tools, and analytical frameworks required to maintain an accurate, continuously updated view of the external landscape.
  • Define and track the competitive landscape across the EHSQ, ESG, and adjacent markets — including product capabilities, positioning, pricing, GTM strategy, and customer win/loss patterns for key competitors and emerging point solutions.
  • Synthesize win/loss analysis, analyst research (Verdantix, Gartner, Forrester), customer feedback, and market data into structured competitive briefs and strategic recommendations for product, sales, and marketing leadership.
  • Monitor market dynamics including regulatory developments (CSRD, UFLPA, ISO updates, EPA enforcement), emerging technology trends (AI in EHS, supply chain traceability, ESG reporting), and M&A activity across the competitive landscape.
  • Deliver regular executive-level market intelligence briefings, competitive positioning updates, and strategic threat/opportunity assessments to the CPTO and senior leadership team.

  • Partner with Sales Enablement to translate competitive intelligence into sales battlecards, objection handling frameworks, and competitive response playbooks.

4. Product Strategy and Strategic Planning

  • Contribute to Intelex's annual and multi-year product strategy, integrating market intelligence, competitive positioning, and inorganic growth opportunities into a coherent strategic narrative.
  • Lead strategic analysis of new market entry opportunities — including vertical expansion, geographic growth, and adjacent product categories — providing data-driven investment recommendations.
  • Own the product portfolio analysis framework, helping leadership make informed decisions on where to invest, expand, hold, or divest across the product catalog.
  • Partner with the Product Management leadership team to ensure organic roadmap priorities are informed by external market data and aligned with inorganic growth strategy.

  • Represent Intelex externally at industry analyst briefings, customer advisory boards, and market events as a strategic spokesperson for product direction and market positioning.

5. Stakeholder Management and Cross-functional Leadership

  • Build strong working relationships with the CPTO, CEO, and executive leadership team, operating as a trusted strategic advisor on market, competitive, and inorganic growth matters.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Management, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Legal, and Corporate Development to ensure strategic initiatives are resourced, aligned, and executed with rigor.
  • Present complex strategic analyses and recommendations with clarity and conviction to senior leadership, the Board, and external stakeholders.
  • Lead and develop a small team of analysts and intelligence specialists, building organizational capability in market research, competitive analysis, and strategic due diligence.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline required. MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.
  • 8+ years of experience in product strategy, corporate development, strategy consulting, or a combination thereof within enterprise SaaS or technology markets.
  • Demonstrated experience owning or significantly contributing to M&A processes, including target identification, due diligence, and integration planning.
  • Proven track record in building and managing technology partnerships, including commercial negotiation and joint go-to-market execution.
  • Deep knowledge of the EHSQ and ESG markets strongly preferred. Familiarity with Intelex's competitive landscape is a significant advantage.
  • Experience building or leading a market intelligence or competitive intelligence function, including analyst relations management.

Skills and Abilities

  • Exceptional strategic thinking — able to synthesize complex market, competitive, and financial data into clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Strong commercial acumen with experience structuring and evaluating technology partnerships and acquisition opportunities.
  • Deep product intuition — able to assess product-market fit, technology architecture, and integration complexity of potential M&A and partnership candidates.
  • Outstanding communication and executive presence — comfortable presenting strategic recommendations to C-suite and Board-level audiences.
  • Data-driven analyst mindset with experience building competitive intelligence frameworks, win/loss programs, and market sizing models.
  • Ability to operate with autonomy in ambiguous, high-stakes situations while maintaining strong cross-functional alignment.
  • Strong negotiation skills with experience leading commercial discussions with external technology partners, vendors, and acquisition targets.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working with enterprise software analyst firms (Verdantix, Gartner, Forrester) in a product or strategy capacity.
  • Familiarity with regulatory frameworks driving EHSQ and ESG software demand: CSRD, UFLPA, ISO 45001, EPA PSM, OSHA, FDA 21 CFR.
  • Experience in a high-growth SaaS environment with exposure to both organic product development and inorganic growth motions.
  • Existing network within the EHSQ, safety, ESG, or industrial software ecosystem.

Why Intelex?

  • Strategic Impact: Shape how Intelex grows beyond its organic portfolio — owning the decisions that define the company's competitive position for the next decade.
  • Market Leadership: Join a company with 1,400+ customers across 30+ countries operating in the fastest-growing segments of enterprise software — ESG, AI-enabled safety analytics, and supply chain compliance.
  • Purpose-Driven Mission: Work on products that contribute to a safer, more sustainable world by empowering organizations to make smarter, more responsible decisions.
  • Executive Visibility: Report directly to the CPTO and work in close partnership with the CEO and executive leadership on the company's most strategically consequential decisions.
  • Culture: Join a diverse, inclusive, and energetic team recognized as one of Canada's Top Places to Work, with a culture that values collaboration, intellectual rigor, and continuous learning.

description:
Summary:

Operates a forklift to stack and retrieve supplies and materials. Responsibilities also include documenting and maintaining inventory and ensuring production area organization and cleanliness.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Adheres to all safety policies and procedures
  • Obeys all Cal/OSHA guidelines and regulations
  • Ensures equipment is in safe operating condition
  • Moves pallets from one area to another
  • Ensures that pallets and boxes are properly accounted for
  • Ensures that daily inspections of equipment are completed before utilization
  • Maintains clear and open communication with management
  • General warehouse duties as needed
  • Perform a combination of the following duties including but not limited to:
  • Must follow product rotation procedures, and organization while using internal day code system
    Inspect all trailers before loading for any issues (ie damage, torn chute, foul smell…)
  • Verify order number and truck name with line truck driver prior to loading
  • Learn and understand the various loading configurations, and patterns of product / commodities
  • Load transport vehicles, making sure loads are evenly and securely placed
  • Load trailers safely and properly while using standard loading procedures / patterns without damaging produce, boxes, or trailer equip
  • Must understand weight distribution on long haul trailers and demonstrate loading capabilities (ie loading and stacking techniques, including separating wet and dry goods)
  • Document on loading manifest the exact quantities of all commodities loaded into trailer, as well as any additional services performed (ie stacking, bagging, and corner boarding)
  • Must be able to read and follow loading instructions, and communicate with line truck drivers any weight restrictions / limits
  • Assist dispatch office with product availability to help schedule truck loading
  • Follow safe operating procedures
  • Maintain a clean work area, and material handling
  • Keep a record of daily operations
  • Service and make minor adjustments to the forklift
  • Must be able to work flexible hours in a cold environment (33 Deg F / 1 Deg C)
  • Practice the “honor system” – be forthright and honest under all circumstances
  • Suggest opportunities for improvement
  • Fill out pre-start up forklift inspection form- Report any issues to your immediate supervisor
  • Inspect the inside of the trailer before loading, and fill out the trailer inspection section on the pick ticket (loading manifest). Contact a supervisor if the walls or air chute are damaged; mark the number of pallets already on board of trailer, if any.
  • Read the loading manifest and read the loading instructions before loading
  • Load on a FIFO (Fist in, First out) basis unless stated otherwise on pick ticket (manifest)
  • Load by lot specified on the loading manifest
  • Only pull daughter tags for product that are the forks of the forklift. Do Not pull more daughter tags from pallets that are not being handled. Load pallets that have daughter tags pulled off and report it on the loading schematics
  • Verify that the amount ordered on the pick ticket (manifest) matches the amount reported on the loading schematics
  • Report placement of the recorder on the loading schematics with a “R” on orders that call for a recorder
    Verify that the recorder is started and place it in the trailer. Please place it on dry cartons and not on top of any iced product
    Verify that the truck driver secures the pallets loaded with load locks
  • Fold the dock leveler (ramp) and close the roll up door

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees in this position. This is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Cloud Service Mesh
description:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. The CSM (Cloud Service Mesh) Platform is a critical component of Google Cloud's Service Centric Networking, acting as the foundation for AI enablements and next-generation Agentic workloads. Our mission is to create many differentiating features to allow customers to operate their microservices securely, compliantly, and scalably, regardless of the platform they run on or the type of compute infrastructure they need.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

title: Hardware Product Implementation Specialist
description:
At VAS, we develop technology that helps dairy operations use data and connected solutions to improve how they work. We are looking for a Hardware Product Implementation Specialist who enjoys being hands-on with hardware, solving technical problems in the field, and helping customers successfully bring new technology to life. In this role, you will lead customer hardware deployments from planning through installation, training, and post-go-live support.

This role is a great fit for someone who likes variety in their work and believes in delivering an excellent experience for every customer. One week you may be coordinating a deployment plan with a customer and electrical contractor, and the next you may be onsite installing equipment, troubleshooting connectivity, or helping a team get comfortable using a newly implemented system. You will be a key point of contact throughout the implementation process and will play an important role in ensuring customers have a smooth, successful experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead customer hardware deployment projects from planning through installation, testing, commissioning, and handoff.

  • Perform onsite installation, configuration, and troubleshooting of hardware systems, network-connected devices, sensors, control systems, and related equipment.

  • Coordinate with customers, electricians, contractors, vendors, and internal teams to keep projects moving forward.

  • Conduct site assessments, confirm installation requirements, and identify potential risks before deployment.

  • Provide clear project updates, manage timelines, and help resolve issues as they arise.

  • Support customers after implementation through onsite and remote troubleshooting, follow-up visits, and issue resolution.

  • Document installation activities, configurations, customer communications, and support outcomes.

What You’ll Bring

  • At least 2 years of experience in hardware installation, implementation, field services, technical deployment, or a related role.

  • Experience managing customer-facing technical projects from kickoff through completion.

  • Ability to read and interpret installation drawings, site plans, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation.

  • Comfort working directly with electricians, contractors, facility managers, customers, and internal teams.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to stay calm and practical when solving technical issues in the field.

  • Clear communication skills and the ability to keep customers and stakeholders informed.

  • Strong organization skills with the ability to manage multiple projects at once.

  • A valid driver’s license and willingness to travel extensively.

Travel and Work Environment

This role requires frequent domestic and international travel, generally 50% to 75%, based on customer needs and project schedules. The work includes time in customer facilities, field environments, and implementation sites, as well as remote coordination and support. Candidates should be comfortable lifting and carrying equipment up to 50 pounds, working indoors and outdoors, climbing ladders, and supporting installations in commercial, industrial, construction, and customer facility settings.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to own the customer implementation experience for hardware solutions that need to work reliably in real-world environments. You will combine technical execution, project coordination, customer partnership, and problem-solving in a role where your work is visible, practical, and directly tied to customer success.

If you enjoy hands-on technical work, take pride in keeping projects organized, and like building trusted relationships with customers and field partners, this role offers the chance to make a meaningful impact from installation through long-term support.

title: Senior Analyst - Army Training Products
description:

We have employees nationwide and for the past three consecutive years were named one of the fastest growing Veteran-owned companies in the nation. Senior Analyst – Army Training Products

Program: CAC - TMD Army Training Products
Location: Fort Leavenworth, KS / Proponent-Specific Locations
Openings: 9
Experience Level: Senior
Clearance: Active Secret required
Position Type: Key Personnel

Position Summary

MKS2 Technologies is seeking Senior Analysts to support the U.S. Army Combined Arms Center (CAC), Training Management Directorate (TMD), Army Training Products mission.

Senior Analysts will serve as subject matter experts for designated Army proponents, applying branch-specific operational experience and Army training expertise to the development, review, revision, and sustainment of critical Army training products.

This position will support products and initiatives including Combined Arms Training Strategies (CATS), Army Training and Evaluation Program (ARTEP) products, Mission Training Plans (MTPs), Standard Mission Essential Task Lists (METLs), Front End Analyses (FEAs), task crosswalks, and related Army training-readiness products.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as a Senior Analyst and subject matter expert for an assigned Army proponent or functional area.
  • Support the development, review, revision, validation, and sustainment of CATS and other Army training products.
  • Conduct mission and training analysis involving unit missions, capabilities, Mission Essential Tasks, Battle Tasks, collective tasks, individual tasks, and drills.
  • Support the development and review of FEAs, task crosswalks, Standard METL-focused CATS, Training Event Models, and ARTEP/MTP products.
  • Analyze Army doctrine, organizational changes, force structure, training requirements, and modernization initiatives for potential impacts to training products.
  • Coordinate with Army proponents and validation organizations to ensure training products accurately reflect applicable missions, capabilities, tasks, and training requirements.
  • Apply Army Training Management principles to support training strategies and operational readiness.
  • Identify gaps or inconsistencies in unit task lists, collective tasks, supporting tasks, training events, and training resources.
  • Participate in working groups, product reviews, validation events, briefings, conferences, and technical discussions.
  • Review assigned products for accuracy, completeness, doctrinal alignment, and quality.
  • Develop technical analyses, recommendations, briefings, reports, information papers, and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate with Government personnel, Army proponents, operational organizations, and fellow analysts to resolve training-development issues and support timely product delivery.

Required Qualifications

  • Active Secret security clearance at the time of response.
  • Must have been awarded an Army MOS, Branch qualification, or directly related skills applicable to the supported proponent.
  • Must have achieved a minimum military rank of:
    • Major (O-4)
    • Chief Warrant Officer 3 (CW-3)
    • Sergeant First Class (E-7)
  • Bachelor’s degree in any field OR graduate of military professional education equivalent to:
    • Command and General Staff College (CGSC)
    • Sergeant Majors Academy
    • Applicable Army-specific specialty course
  • 5+ years of general experience in one or more of the following:
    • Military planning
    • Training
    • Operations
    • Logistics
    • Intelligence
    • Force design/development
    • Capability development
    • Training development
  • Previous experience serving on a Battalion- or Brigade-level staff in an operations position.
  • Strong knowledge of Army operations, organizations, missions, capabilities, and training requirements applicable to the supported proponent.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, briefing, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with military, Government, and contractor stakeholders.

Preferred Experience

Additional experience with the following is highly desirable:

  • Army Training Management
  • Combined Arms Training Strategies (CATS)
  • Army Training and Evaluation Program (ARTEP)
  • Mission Training Plans (MTPs)
  • Standard Mission Essential Task Lists (METLs)
  • Unit Task Lists and Training & Evaluation Outlines
  • Front End Analysis and task crosswalk development
  • TRADOC Pamphlet 350-70-1
  • FM 7-0
  • AR 350-1
  • ATMS Development Tool
  • Digital Training Management System (DTMS)
  • Army Training Network (ATN)
  • Experience supporting CAC, TRADOC, Army Centers of Excellence, FORSCOM, Army proponents, or operational Army organizations

Supported Proponent Areas

Senior Analysts may provide support aligned to Army proponents and functional areas associated with:

  • FORSCOM
  • Maneuver, including Armor and Infantry
  • Aviation
  • Fires, including Field Artillery and Air Defense Artillery
  • Special Warfare
  • Maneuver Support
  • CASCOM

Candidates supporting individual proponents should possess relevant MOS, Branch, operational, or functional-area expertise aligned to that organization.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is an experienced Army professional who combines significant Battalion/Brigade-level operational experience with a strong understanding of Army training and readiness.

Successful candidates will be able to translate operational and branch-specific expertise into accurate Army training products while collaborating effectively with Army proponents, Government stakeholders, and other subject matter experts.

description:

Distinguished Architect, Enterprise Stability & Resilience Engineering

Job Title

Distinguished Architect, Enterprise Stability & Resilience Engineering

Job Summary

The Distinguished Architect for Enterprise Stability & Resilience Engineering is a senior technical leader responsible for defining and driving the enterprise architecture, engineering capabilities, standards, and strategies that enable resilient, reliable, secure, recoverable, and high-performing customer journeys across the organization.

This role is fundamentally different from traditional enterprise, cloud, infrastructure, platform, or application architecture positions. The successful candidate must be capable of understanding business domains, customer behaviors, end-to-end customer journeys, and complex technology ecosystems to identify systemic risks and architect enterprise-wide resilience capabilities.

The Distinguished Architect will partner closely with the Director of Enterprise Stability & Resilience Engineering to establish the future-state strategy, architecture, governance model, engineering controls, and automation capabilities required to improve operational resilience across the enterprise.

The ideal candidate combines deep software engineering expertise, enterprise architecture leadership, business acumen, and systems thinking to create resilience-by-design, reliability-by-design, security-by-design, and recoverability-by-design capabilities that become embedded into the organization's engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Resilience Architecture

  • Define the enterprise architecture vision and strategy for Stability, Resilience, Reliability, Recoverability, Security, and Performance Engineering.
  • Develop reference architectures, engineering standards, patterns, frameworks, and reusable capabilities that improve enterprise resilience.
  • Architect resilience capabilities across critical customer journeys, business functions, and technology ecosystems.
  • Identify systemic risks, architectural vulnerabilities, concentration risks, failure points, and operational dependencies across the enterprise.

Customer Journey & Business Capability Engineering

  • Develop deep understanding of business domains, customer journeys, customer behaviors, and critical business capabilities.
  • Create end-to-end technology and business capability maps spanning channels, applications, APIs, middleware, data platforms, infrastructure, and third-party services.
  • Analyze customer journeys to identify failure scenarios, recovery gaps, resiliency weaknesses, and customer-impact risks.
  • Influence technology decisions through a customer-outcome and business-value perspective.

Reliability, Recoverability & Performance Engineering

  • Establish enterprise-wide engineering principles for reliability, recoverability, fault tolerance, availability, scalability, and performance.
  • Define architectural patterns for disaster recovery, cyber recovery, workload resilience, service continuity, and operational readiness.
  • Partner with engineering teams to ensure resilience and reliability requirements are integrated into solution designs.
  • Drive engineering approaches that proactively prevent customer-impacting incidents.

Engineering Controls & Automation

  • Define and automate resilience and reliability controls within software delivery pipelines.
  • Establish architecture guardrails, governance-by-design practices, engineering scorecards, and automated stage-gate controls.
  • Reduce dependence on manual governance processes by embedding standards, controls, and policy enforcement directly into engineering workflows.
  • Design measurable resilience and reliability maturity frameworks across customer journeys and technology platforms.

Strategic Technology Leadership

  • Serve as the enterprise thought leader for resilience engineering and customer journey-centered architecture.
  • Influence senior executives, enterprise architects, engineers, and business leaders on resilience strategies and investment priorities.
  • Represent Stability & Resilience Engineering in Architecture Review Boards, executive forums, and strategic planning discussions.
  • Mentor architects and engineering leaders across the organization.

Required Qualifications

  • 15+ years of experience in software engineering, solution architecture, enterprise architecture, or large-scale technology leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated expertise across software engineering, architecture, delivery, and operational excellence.
  • Proven ability to design and influence large-scale enterprise technology ecosystems.
  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, APIs, integration architecture, event-driven architectures, middleware, data platforms, and enterprise application landscapes.
  • Experience designing highly available, fault-tolerant, resilient, and recoverable systems.
  • Deep understanding of business capability modeling and customer journey architecture.
  • Strong executive communication, influencing, and strategic leadership skills.
  • Exceptional systems-thinking capabilities with an ability to connect technology decisions to business outcomes and customer impact.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Financial services, banking, payments, or highly regulated industry experience.
  • Experience leading customer-journey-centric transformation initiatives.
  • Experience in resilience engineering, reliability engineering, performance engineering, operational resilience, disaster recovery, cyber recovery, and risk management.
  • Experience defining enterprise engineering standards, governance frameworks, and architecture maturity models.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence enterprise-wide engineering and architecture practices.
  • Experience creating engineering platforms, automated controls, and governance-by-design capabilities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a rare architect and engineering leader who:

  • Thinks in customer journeys rather than individual systems.
  • Understands business domains as deeply as technical domains.
  • Can identify hidden risks and systemic weaknesses across complex ecosystems.
  • Architects resilience, reliability, security, recoverability, and performance as enterprise capabilities.
  • Creates standards, patterns, controls, and automation that scale across the organization.
  • Bridges executive strategy, enterprise architecture, engineering execution, and operational outcomes.
  • Drives resilience-by-design and reliability-by-design across the software development lifecycle.

title: Medior / Senior Data Engineer
description:
Bij Aizy bouwen we software waarmee agencies en webshops hun online advertenties beheren. Ons platform verzamelt campagneresultaten, doet aanbevelingen met AI en kan automatisch wijzigingen uitvoeren in advertentieaccounts.

Die aanbevelingen worden zo goed als de data eronder. We bouwen daarom een beslismotor die leert van alles wat we weten over een klant: campagneresultaten, wat de klant ons heeft verteld en wat er eerder werkte. We zoeken een data engineer die de basis daarvoor legt. Jij zorgt dat alle data betrouwbaar binnenkomt, goed gemodelleerd is en klaarstaat voor ons AI-team.

Medior / Senior Data Engineer @aizy

(Python en SQL)

Breda · 40 uur · Op kantoor in Breda · Medior of senior

Bij Aizy bouwen we software waarmee agencies en webshops hun online advertenties beheren. Ons platform verzamelt campagneresultaten, doet aanbevelingen met AI en kan automatisch wijzigingen uitvoeren in advertentieaccounts.

Die aanbevelingen worden zo goed als de data eronder. We bouwen daarom een beslismotor die leert van alles wat we weten over een klant: campagneresultaten, wat de klant ons heeft verteld en wat er eerder werkte. We zoeken een data engineer die de basis daarvoor legt. Jij zorgt dat alle data betrouwbaar binnenkomt, goed gemodelleerd is en klaarstaat voor ons AI-team.

Wat je gaat doen

Je bouwt ons dataplatform op, grotendeels vanaf de basis. Je haalt data binnen uit Google Ads, Meta, ChatGPT Ads en andere kanalen, maar ook uit wat klanten met onze AI‑assistant bespreken en wat het platform over elke klant onthoudt. Die data breng je samen in een warehouse of lake, zodat het AI‑team er modellen en beslissingen op kan bouwen.

  • Datapijplijnen bouwen die campagnedata, klantgeheugen, gesprekken met onze AI‑assistant en andere bronnen betrouwbaar en op tijd binnenhalen.
  • Een datamodel ontwerpen dat klanten, merken, kanalen en campagnes eenduidig met elkaar verbindt, ook als platformen andere begrippen gebruiken.
  • De opslag inrichten: wat in PostgreSQL blijft, wat naar een warehouse of lake gaat, en hoe historie bewaard blijft.
  • Data beschikbaar maken voor de beslismotor, dashboards en onze AI‑assistant, via goed gedocumenteerde tabellen, views of API’s.
  • Datakwaliteit bewaken: ontbrekende dagen, dubbele records en afwijkende cijfers zien voordat een klant of een model ze ziet.
  • Klantdata goed scheiden en zorgvuldig omgaan met gesprekken en persoonsgegevens.

Daarnaast werk je mee aan de beslismotor zelf. Samen met onze AI engineer bouw je features, test je of aanbevelingen kloppen en meet je wat ze in de praktijk opleveren. Dat is niet je hoofdtaak, maar je kunt er wel zelfstandig aan bijdragen.

Onze stack en werkwijze

De backend draait op Python, FastAPI en PostgreSQL, met een aparte worker voor geplande taken. We halen data op via de SDK's van Google Ads en Meta en gebruiken Claude voor onze AI‑functies. De frontend is gebouwd met TypeScript, SvelteKit en Tailwind. We gebruiken Docker voor de ontwikkelomgeving.

Voor het dataplatform ligt nog niet alles vast. Welke warehouse‑ of lake‑oplossing, welke tooling voor transformaties en orkestratie: daar bepaal jij mee de keuze. We zoeken iets dat past bij ons team en mee kan groeien.

We werken dagelijks met AI‑agents zoals Claude Code en Codex. We zoeken iemand voor wie AI een vanzelfsprekend onderdeel van ontwikkelen is, die de mogelijkheden volgt en graag uitprobeert wat werkt. Jij houdt het overzicht en beoordeelt de kwaliteit van het resultaat.

Heb je een aanpak gevonden die goed werkt? Dan deel je die met het team. Zo verbeteren we samen onze manier van ontwikkelen.

Wat je meebrengt

  • Je hebt ervaring met het bouwen en onderhouden van datapijplijnen die in productie draaien.
  • Je hebt een stevige basis in Python en bent sterk in SQL.
  • Je kunt een datamodel ontwerpen dat begrijpelijk blijft voor anderen, bijvoorbeeld met een dimensioneel model of een medallion-opzet.
  • Je hebt gewerkt aan datasystemen die op schaal in productie draaien, van opslag tot transformatie en orkestratie.
  • Je hebt data uit externe API’s gehaald en weet hoe je omgaat met rate limits, wijzigende schema’s en het opnieuw ophalen van historie.
  • Je houdt rekening met privacy, klantdata en de AVG.
  • Je bent nieuwsgierig naar hoe AI‑modellen data gebruiken en wilt meebouwen aan de beslismotor.
  • Je omarmt AI als onderdeel van je vak en zoekt actief naar manieren om er beter en sneller mee te werken.
  • Je vindt het prettig om met collega’s op kantoor in Breda samen te werken.
  • Nederlands is onze voertaal op kantoor. Je spreekt en begrijpt het goed genoeg om makkelijk mee te doen aan overleg, technische discussies en gesprekken tussendoor.

Pluspunten zijn ervaring met advertentiedata van Google Ads of Meta, met ongestructureerde data zoals gesprekken of tekst, en met feature stores of embeddings.

Je hoeft niet alles te kennen. We horen vooral graag wat je hebt gebouwd, welke keuzes je hebt gemaakt en wat je daarvan hebt geleerd.

Wat je bij ons krijgt

  • Salaris tussen €4.600 en €7.000 op basis van ervaring
  • Een gezellig team met korte lijnen. We werken samen op kantoor in Breda, helpen elkaar en hebben ook ruimte voor een goed gesprek tussendoor.
  • Een dataplatform dat je zelf mag opzetten. Je bepaalt mee welke keuzes we maken en waarom.
  • Ruimte om te groeien, bijvoorbeeld richting data‑architectuur of machine learning, en meer technische verantwoordelijkheid naarmate het bedrijf groeit.
  • Werk aan een eigen product. Je ziet direct hoe jouw data de aanbevelingen voor klanten beter maakt.
  • Ruimte om volop met AI te werken. Wat goed werkt, nemen we samen over.
  • We zijn een groeiende startup. Prioriteiten kunnen veranderen en er is nog veel te bouwen. Dat geeft je veel ruimte om mee te bepalen hoe het product en het team zich ontwikkelen.

ONLY DUTCH NATIVE SPEAKERS

ONLY DUTCH RESIDENTS

NO RECRUITERS

title: Devops engineer
description:
Omschrijving

Opdrachtomschrijving
Als Devops engineer maak je deel uit van een multidisciplinair technisch projectteam dat verantwoordelijk is voor de voorbereiding en technische validatie van de erfpachtketen in het algemeen en Hermes in het bijzonder, binnen de gemeentelijke informatievoorziening.
Je wordt ingezet voor de analyse van bestaande Enterprise-applicaties, maatwerkcomponenten en technische afhankelijkheden. Daarbij breng je de huidige applicatiearchitectuur in kaart, beoordeel je de impact van technische wijzigingen en lever je een belangrijke bijdrage aan de voorbereiding van migratie-, moderniserings- en lifecycletrajecten.
Je werkt nauw samen met solution architecten, ontwikkelaars, functioneel beheerders, beheerteams, infrastructuurspecialisten en leveranciers. Vanuit jouw technische expertise adviseer je over de uitvoerbaarheid van wijzigingen, de impact op het applicatielandschap en de benodigde maatregelen om een veilige en beheersbare transitie mogelijk te maken.
Wij zijn op zoek naar een ervaren Senior Application Engineer met ruime kennis van complexe Enterprise-applicaties, softwareontwikkeling, integraties en lifecycle management binnen de erfpachtketen in het algemeen en Hermes in het bijzonder. Je bent analytisch sterk, beschikt over brede technische kennis en bent in staat om complexe applicatielandschappen te vertalen naar heldere analyses en concrete adviezen.
Werkzaamheden

  • Analyseren en documenteren van de bestaande applicatiearchitectuur en technische inrichting.
  • Inventariseren en beoordelen van maatwerkcomponenten en de technische kwaliteit hiervan.
  • Analyseren van interfaces, API's en koppelingen met interne en externe systemen.
  • Vaststellen en documenteren van technische afhankelijkheden binnen het applicatielandschap.
  • Uitvoeren van impactanalyses ten aanzien van migraties, upgrades en technische wijzigingen.
  • Ondersteunen bij de ontwikkeling van een teststrategie.
  • Bijdragen aan technische validaties en uitvoerbaarheidsanalyses.
  • Adviseren over de technische uitvoerbaarheid van voorgestelde oplossingsrichtingen
  • Signaleren van technische risico's, knelpunten en aandachtspunten binnen het applicatielandschap.
  • Afstemmen met architecten, ontwikkelaars, beheerders, leveranciers en overige technische stakeholders.


Gemeentelijke organisatie
De gemeentelijke organisatie bestaat uit 5 clusters, een bestuurs- en concernstaf, 7 stadsdelen en 1 stadsgebied. De stadsdelen besturen samen met de gemeenteraad, burgemeester en wethouders de stad Amsterdam. De 5 clusters zijn: Ruimte en Economie, Sociaal, Stadbeheer, Bedrijfsvoering, Digitalisering, Innovatie en Informatie. De clusters hebben expertise op een specifiek terrein, zoals sport, jeugd of parkeren. Zij werken beleid uit tot stadsbrede kaders waarbinnen de stadsdelen het uitvoerende werk kunnen doen. Ook bieden zij directe ondersteuning aan bewoners die dit nodig hebben, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van participatie of werk. De stadsdelen houden zich onder andere bezig met de inrichting van straten en pleinen, groen en parken en welzijnswerk in de buurt. Ze zorgen ervoor dat wat ze doen, past bij de behoeften in hun stadsdeel en bij het beleid voor de hele stad. Meer informatie over de gemeentelijke organisatie is te vinden op: https://www.amsterdam.nl/.
De opdrachtgever
De afdeling Informatievoorziening werkt voor het gehele Cluster Ruimte en Economie en ondersteunt de directies binnen het cluster met betrouwbare en toekomstbestendige informatievoorziening. De afdeling ontwikkelt, beheert en vernieuwt de applicaties en IT-voorzieningen die burgers, bedrijven en medewerkers ondersteunen bij de uitvoering van gemeentelijke dienstverlening op het gebied van erfpacht en uitgifte. Binnen Informatievoorziening Erfpacht & Uitgifte is het VES-team verantwoordelijk voor het beheer, de doorontwikkeling en de technische continuïteit van een aantal bedrijfskritische applicaties die de primaire processen van de directie Erfpacht & Uitgifte ondersteunen. De medewerkers werken in multidisciplinaire Agile-teams waarin beheer, ontwikkeling en vernieuwing van de informatievoorziening integraal worden uitgevoerd. De komende periode staat de organisatie voor een omvangrijk technisch voorbereidings- en validatietraject gericht op de continuïteit en toekomstbestendigheid van het applicatielandschap. In dit kader worden tijdelijke gespecialiseerde professionals ingezet voor het uitvoeren van technische analyses, architectuurvalidaties, platformonderzoeken.

title: Distinguished Software Engineer
description:
Credit Acceptance is proud to be an award-winning company recognized both locally and nationally across multiple workplace categories. Our world-class culture is shaped by dedicated team members who are driven to succeed as professionals individually and together as a team. Backed by a strong product, exceptional people, and a stable financial foundation, we’ve grown into a leading provider of used and new car financing across the country.

Our Engineering and Analytics Team Members utilize the latest technology to develop, monitor, and maintain complex practices that help optimize our success. Our Team Members value being challenged, are encouraged to express their ideas, and have the flexibility to enjoy work life balance. We build intrinsic value by partnering with all functions of our business to support their success and make strategic business decisions. We focus on professional development and continuous improvement while enjoying a casual work environment and Great Place to Work culture!

Credit Acceptance makes vehicle ownership possible for consumers other lenders decline, through a dealer network, an originations and servicing platform, and pricing and decisioning models refined over decades. The technology estate underneath this business was built project by project over a long period, and modernizing it is the largest engineering opportunity at the company. As the Distinguished Engineer, you are the senior-most individual contributor in Technology, reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer. You will set the multi-year technical strategy for the company while staying close enough to the code and systems to remain credible — this is not an architect role that reviews designs from a distance, nor a strong engineer role that goes deep in a single domain. Two things sit at the center of the job: the target architecture for the enterprise, and the architecture for running AI agents across it. You will not own a team; you will own the hardest technical problems the company has, and get them resolved by convincing the people who do own the teams.

Outcomes and Activities

  • Enterprise target architecture: Convene the principal and staff engineers who own each domain to define the end-state architecture across originations, servicing, marketplace, data, and AI, and use it to drive the multi-year plan. Ensure every component has a defined interface with stated inputs and outputs, every unmade decision has a written principle standing in for it, and the document states honestly how close the organization is to the end state. Publish the architecture, including the tradeoffs that were rejected and why.
  • Agentic AI architecture across the enterprise: Own the enterprise agent architecture spanning servicing and collections, the dealer side, originations, and internal engineering and back-office workflows, built on one common foundation rather than one stack per team. Establish a governed way for agents to discover and call business capabilities, data, and tools, using the Model Context Protocol as the integration layer. Define an identity and authorization model that treats an agent as a first-class actor with its own least-privilege entitlements, along with observability, evaluation, and cost controls that work consistently for every agent. Set policy on what an agent may decide independently versus what stays with a person, and define where that line moves and on what evidence. Design the architecture to produce an examiner-ready record of what each agent saw, recommended, and touched, and set the evaluation and adversarial testing approach that makes agent outcomes defensible. Ensure the same foundation and controls apply to agents built by outside firms on the company's behalf.
  • Migration off on-premises infrastructure: Own the technical strategy for migrating transactional and analytical workloads off on-premises infrastructure to the company's strategic targets — AWS for transactional workloads and Databricks for analytical workloads — determining what lifts and shifts, what replatforms, what gets re-architected on the way versus after, and what the steady-state cost looks like. Own the resilience and recovery architecture for the target state.
  • Data platform architecture: Set the architecture for change-data-capture-based ingestion, streaming where warranted, and a modern warehouse with no job-scheduling dependency, moving the organization from largely batch analytical data movement to real time. Help settle the open question of who owns the transactional and analytical data models.
  • Real-time decisioning, model serving, and experimentation: Architect for pricing and credit model and scorecard updates that drop in as a layer rather than requiring a multi-quarter rebuild, and for an experimentation platform that supports orders of magnitude more concurrent experiments than a conventional release process allows.
  • Marketplace and search architecture: Own the architecture and interfaces for a unified vehicle inventory, consumer search, and lead routing platform, ensuring the data model supports more than one class of seller from the start.
  • AI-native engineering practice: Define the golden path for how software is specified, generated, reviewed, tested, and deployed, including the analyzers and gates that enforce it, and measure the inputs to that practice rather than just the outputs. Hold the build-versus-buy bar for AI capability, building what is core competency and about to scale, and renting the rest.
  • Performance and peak readiness: Own the instrumentation, baseline, and remediation architecture needed to meet the standard that no page takes more than one second. Own peak-event headroom, including understanding the limits of each system and maintaining tested degradation levers ahead of need.
  • Operating approach: Move the organization from project-shaped systems toward owned platforms with stated contracts. Document every component's inputs and outputs, and be ready to argue why closely coupled components should not be consolidated into one. Work toward a two-week requirement-to-production iteration bar, treating architecture that cannot be delivered incrementally as unfinished. Name what comes off the plan whenever a change in direction is requested. Make the call and own the outcome on architectural recommendations. Treat security, privacy, auditability, and regulatory obligation as design inputs from the start in this regulated environment.
  • Hands-on, not hands-off: This is not optional. Stay personally engaged in the technical work rather than directing it from a distance. Join design reviews, write proofs of concept, read code, and engage in incident analysis. This hands-on time does not replace the work the teams own, and it is not a fallback when delivery slips. Every engineer in the organization will read how you write, how you argue a design, how you handle being wrong, and how you treat engineers who disagree with you as the bar. Staff and principal engineers should be measurably better at this work for having worked with you.
  • Success measures: A published target architecture the domain owners agree with and that the annual and long-range plans are actually written against; an enterprise agent foundation that internal teams and partners build on, with access controls, evaluation, and audit records in place; a credible, dated, costed migration path off on-premises infrastructure and demonstrated progress against it; measured improvement in chosen input metrics such as latency, availability, recovery objectives, deployment frequency, and experiment throughput; growth in the number of principal and staff engineers who are better at this work as a result of this role; and architectural decisions that stop being relitigated because the reasoning was written down and the interfaces were clear.

Competencies

The following items detail how you will be successful in this role. At this level, you are expected to set the standard for each.

  • Customer Empathy: Customer Empathy is the ability to understand the perspectives, pain points, and experiences of customers. It involves actively putting oneself in the customer’s shoes, comprehending their needs and challenges, and using that understanding to provide a better, more customer-centric experience.
  • Engineering Excellence: Engineering Excellence is about bringing great craftsmanship and thought leadership to deliver an outstanding product that delights customers and solves for the business. This involves the pursuit and achievement of high standards, best practices, innovation, and superior solutions.
  • One Team: A One Team mindset refers to a collaborative approach across the organization, where individuals work together seamlessly, without boundaries, as a single, cohesive team. Shared goals, open communication and mutual support create a sense of collective purpose. This enables teams to navigate challenges and pursue shared objectives more effectively.
  • Owner’s Mindset: Owner’s Mindset involves adopting a set of behaviors that reflect a sense of responsibility, accountability, strategic thinking, and a proactive approach to managing your domain. As an owner, you understand the business and your domain(s) deeply and solve for the right outcome for the domain(s) and the business.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or closely related field of study; or equivalent work experience
  • Minimum 10 years of software engineering experience or comparable depth of experience
  • A track record of setting and delivering multi-year technical strategy at enterprise scale, as an individual contributor rather than through a reporting line.
  • Depth in distributed systems architecture, and in at least two of: agentic or LLM-based systems in production; large-scale cloud migration of transactional systems; modern data platform and lakehouse architecture; machine learning platform and model serving; high-traffic consumer or marketplace applications.
  • Architecture ownership of agentic or LLM-based systems that reached production, including how tool and data access were governed, how the system was evaluated, and what its failure modes turned out to be.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a legacy-to-modern migration of systems the business runs on, including the sequencing, the cost case, and the failure modes, with production revenue at stake rather than only familiarity with the concept.
  • Hands-on credibility today: actively reads code, writes proofs of concept, joins design reviews, and participates in incident analysis.
  • Evidence of influence without authority across organizational boundaries, including work that changed direction at the executive level.
  • Strong written communication; architecture here is carried by documents that other people can act on without the author in the room.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop staff and principal engineers, and to raise the technical bar of engineers not directly managed.
  • Experience delivering in a regulated industry, or a clear ability to work inside audit, security, and compliance constraints without treating them as an obstacle.

Preferred Experience

  • Recognized contribution beyond one employer, such as open source, standards work, publications, patents, or a sustained external technical presence.
  • Consumer lending, auto finance, insurance, or payments experience; or large-scale distributed systems experience supporting a business-critical function in another high-stakes domain.
  • The Model Context Protocol or comparable agent tool-integration standards, and identity and authorization design for non-human actors.
  • AWS and Databricks at production scale.
  • Experience standing up an experimentation platform, or moving an organization from tens to thousands of experiments per year.
  • Experience building AI-native development practice across a large engineering organization, and measuring whether it worked.
  • Marketplace, search, or inventory systems with more than one class of seller.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Distributed Systems Mastery: Technical mastery across distributed systems and software architecture, with deep knowledge of current and emerging technologies and their business implications.
  • Enterprise Problem-Solving: Ability to solve enterprise-wide problems where no precedent exists and to own cross-team shared infrastructure.
  • Strategic Independence: Ability to define and execute technical strategy for the entire organization, partner closely with executives, mobilize resources, and drive consensus across stakeholders at all levels.
  • Visionary Leadership: Bold strategic thinking paired with curiosity, ingenuity, and resourcefulness; recognized industry-level thought leadership and a commitment to lifelong learning.
  • Customer and Market Insight: Company-wide expertise in customer needs, using deep customer and market understanding to shape product and technical strategy and anticipate the impact of industry trends.
  • Technical Writing: Ability to produce architecture documentation clear and complete enough for others to act on independently.
  • Executive Communication and Influence: Ability to build consensus and influence direction across organizational and executive boundaries without formal authority.
  • Talent Development: Ability to raise the technical bar of engineers across the organization, including staff and principal engineers who are not direct reports.

Target Compensation: A competitive base salary range from $232,500 - $341,000. This position is eligible for equity and annual cash bonuses. Final compensation within the range is influenced by many factors including role-specific skills, depth and experience level, industry background, relevant education and certifications.


Candidates who reside in the following major metropolitan areas may be eligible for a premium on top of the posted range based on their specific zone: San Francisco, Seattle, Boston, New York City, Los Angeles and San Diego.
